title: Ford Ranger Engines by Year
description: Every factory engine in the Ford Ranger by year: Lima fours, Cologne and Vulcan V6s, the 4.0 V6s, two early diesels, the Ranger EV and the EcoBoost engines.
intro: Ford sold the compact Ranger in the US from 1983 to 2011, then brought back a midsize Ranger for 2019. There was no US model for 2012–2018. The Mazda B-series twin is not included.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

The first Ranger used the 2.0 and 2.3 Lima fours, the 2.8 and 2.9 Cologne V6s and two diesels: a Perkins 2.2 for 1983–1984 and a Mitsubishi 2.3 turbodiesel for 1985–1987. The 4.0 V6 arrived for 1990 and the 3.0 Vulcan V6 for 1991.
The 2.3 four, the 3.0 and the 4.0 V6.
The 2.5 four replaced the 2.3 for 1998, and the 2.3 Duratec four and the overhead-cam 4.0 V6 arrived for 2001. Ford also sold an electric Ranger EV for 1998–2001.
The returning Ranger used the 2.3 EcoBoost four.
The current Ranger adds the 2.7 EcoBoost V6, and the Ranger Raptor uses a 3.0 EcoBoost V6.
